slides.title: An open agent ecosystem
lines: Agents that can do useful work
narration: Astral Deep is an open ecosystem for agents that can do useful work.
We're building it around a simple goal: people should understand what an agent can do, even when it delegates.

slides.title: Authority follows the task
narration: An agent may discover a tool, ask another agent for help, or act on sensitive information.
Each step needs a clear identity and permission boundary.
Finding a capability should never grant permission to use it.

slides.title: Bounded delegation with LETS
narration: With LETS enforcement enabled, delegation has explicit limits.
A child lease receives only a bounded share of its parent's authority and resource budget, with an expiry.
The executor verifies and durably claims a receipt before the protected action.

slides.title: Checks at the action boundary
narration: Astral Deep's design keeps identity, tool policy, and owner isolation on the normal dispatch path.
Sensitive actions need the appropriate checks and confirmation.
Audit provenance helps explain who authorized an action and how authority reached it.

slides.title: Generative UI with primitives
narration: Useful agents also need useful interfaces.
A model can propose a form, table, or chart using structured UI primitives.
Code checks component types and references, bounds the layout, and escapes web content before rendering.
The model proposes. Code decides.

slides.title: One contract across clients
narration: Astral Primitives defines the vocabulary.
Astral Projection renders and adapts it for web and native clients.
Astral Deep orchestrates the work, while Astral Plane owns durable state.
The goal is consistent meaning across devices, with components other developers can reuse.

slides.title: Open protocols and reusable parts
narration: We want these parts to connect through standard M C P, Agent to Agent, and other agent communication protocols.
That means versioned contracts, compatibility tests, and examples that work outside the full Astral stack.

slides.title: Work that moves this forward
narration: There is concrete work to do.
Help test delegation boundaries, improve protocol compatibility, or make voice survive interruptions and reconnects, especially on mobile.
Better primitive rendering, client parity, and independent examples can make the system useful to more developers.

slides.title: A place to contribute
narration: The bounty board turns these goals into tasks across five repositories.
Accepted, reviewed work earns recognition points on the leaderboard.
Join us at astral deep dot github dot I O.

states.title: Agents doing useful work
states.description: A person supplies a task, an agent works, and a summary returns.

states.title: Authority people can follow
states.description: The agent delegates selected-file reading to a helper.

states.title: Discovery finds capabilities
states.description: Discovery exposes tools but grants no authority.

states.title: A separate permission boundary
states.description: Host authorization permits the selected-file read.

states.title: A visible tool can still be denied
states.description: The email tool is discoverable but the helper has no grant to invoke it.

states.title: LETS bounds delegated authority
states.description: A child grant begins within the parent authority.

states.title: The child receives a narrower grant
states.description: Selected-file access is bounded by application authorization and bound arguments.

states.title: Budget and expiry also shrink
states.description: Illustrative resource units and expiry: the child receives 3 of the parent 10 units and ends sooner.

states.title: A receipt comes before the action
states.description: The executor verifies and durably claims the receipt. An invalid or replayed receipt denies the path.

states.title: The protected action follows the claim
states.description: A successful receipt claim permits the protected action to proceed through its remaining authorization checks.

states.title: Checks stay on the dispatch path
states.description: Identity, owner isolation and tool policy are checked on normal dispatch.

states.title: Sensitive actions need confirmation
states.description: Required confirmation remains a gate rather than a model decision.

states.title: Audit records the authority path
states.description: Provenance preserves who authorized the chain and how the action received authority.

states.title: Useful agents need useful interfaces
states.description: A summary form connects the same example task to generative UI.

states.title: The model proposes primitive structure
states.description: The proposal uses actual container, input and button component types.

states.title: Code validates the proposal
states.description: Component types, references, layout bounds and web escaping stay under deterministic code.

states.title: The renderer controls the output
states.description: Only the checked structure becomes a rendered form. This is a schematic, not a product screenshot.

states.title: The model proposes. Code decides.
states.description: The final form uses the same allowed action rather than letting a model supply arbitrary web code.

states.title: A shared UI vocabulary
states.description: Primitives owns the definitions that Projection consumes.

states.title: Projection adapts the same contract
states.description: Projection renders the contract on web, desktop and mobile.

states.title: Each component owns its part
states.description: Deep orchestrates work and Plane owns durable state.

states.title: Same meaning, layouts that fit
states.description: The same input and action appear side by side on desktop and stacked on mobile. Schematics show semantic adaptation, not current screenshots.

states.title: Open protocol connections
states.description: Interoperability goal: apps reach tools through MCP and other agents through Agent2Agent.

states.title: Reusable outside the full Astral stack
states.description: Versioned contracts and compatibility tests make independent component use possible. This is an integration goal, not a conformance claim.

states.title: Contributions prove the boundaries
states.description: Contribution work should test both successful requests and denied authority.

states.title: Mobile voice needs recovery
states.description: Mobile voice contribution goal: interruption and reconnection should preserve the conversation.

states.title: A component others can reuse
states.description: Client parity and independent examples make the shared vocabulary useful to other developers.

states.title: 49 tasks across five repositories
states.description: The board currently contains the 49 owner-approved public source tasks.

states.title: Reviewed work earns recognition
states.description: A successful main merge that closes an approved bounty credits the PR author. No invented contributor scores appear.

states.title: Help move the project forward
states.description: The site is the entry point for public point bounties.
